items.title: John E. Wood Interview, 1986-06-26
items.q: I don't know, what is it, that, the fellow's name, that plays the clarinet down there, who's an Englishman, been around for a while. Chris Burke.

ctx.x: Have you gone to, Decatur Street, from the beginning?

Just sort of, wandered by, and to the, to the gazebo, and to the, Cafe Mediterranean, you know, I usually wander over there, and listen to what's going on, after I've heard, whatever's at the tent, and sometimes, the music is really, pretty good. Sometimes, I don't like it much. It depends, maybe on, my mood, and maybe how many beers, I've had, by the afternoon, and where it's on, but, then at the gazebo, some of that music, is pretty good. I've enjoyed, John Royan's piano playing, right much down there, and, I…
in the front. That's him, yeah. No, no, I just wondered, how that compared, with the music, of years gone by, if any of the bands, down there, sound like the old-timey band.
